story: Show HN: What do you think of this short End User Licensing Agreement?
text: That doesn't work at all if it is the actual wording. For point 1 you can find warranty wording in any number of open source or creative commons licenses. For the second, objectionable requires a definition. For example many would consider the US drone assassination program objectionable, and hence tar US companies and people with the same brush. Does that mean US companies and people can use the software? How many steps do they have to be removed (eg is providing the payroll software to the defense contractor a problem?) [LINK] [VIDEO] Because of copyright laws, people can do virtually nothing with software. If you actually want to give the user freedoms - see [LINK] - then pick a well known free software license since it will have already addressed all these issues.

story: In the bad old days we had Punchcards. How did people deal with that?
text: When you know that history, IBM asking for an exemption to the JSLint license becomes less funny. Watch [VIDEO] (2 minutes) to hear the story from the developer's point of view. Then consider how many totalitarian states today are using IBM computers to track their population. The developer might not realize it, but IBM lawyers absolutely know that they can be fairly accused of using JSLint for evil.
